title: Choose the Plexus sign-in composition
question: Each direction keeps the same secure workflow and Plexus identity. Choose the spatial idea that should lead the redesign.

options.label: The Access Invitation
options.lineage: formal cross-border programme invitations and arrival credentials
options.thesis: Sign-in becomes a precise invitation into a governed business workspace, not a generic account card.
options.viewport: A full-height midnight slate carries the Plexus identity and one accountable route; a mineral credential sheet docks into its lower-right edge with the sign-in task already in focus.
options.risk: The invitation metaphor must remain operational and avoid feeling ceremonial or exclusive.

options.label: The Governed Checkpoint
options.lineage: border-control wayfinding and trusted access checkpoints
options.thesis: The page makes identity verification feel like a calm, legible threshold between public space and protected work.
options.viewport: One continuous dark field is bisected by a bright route line; the form sits directly at the transfer point while workspace context and support occupy the two ends.
options.risk: A literal checkpoint can feel severe unless the copy and spacing keep it calm and welcoming.

options.label: The Workspace Manifest
options.lineage: programme control rooms and departure manifests
options.thesis: Sign-in reads as the first concise line in an accountable operating sequence.
options.viewport: A pale manifest spans the page with three ruled stages—identity, workspace, next action—and the credential form occupies the active first stage beside a midnight brand bay.
options.risk: Its density could feel more administrative than reassuring on a first login.
